The test image shows a very young soybean seedling that has completely wilted and collapsed at soil level. Key features:
- Seedling at cotyledon/early true-leaf stage
- Complete wilting/collapse with leaves drooping to the ground
- Yellowed/browning tissue
- Sandy soil
- Stem appears bent/collapsed near soil line

Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off**, **Rhizoctonia**, **Phytophthora** — all cause seedling collapse. Let me check reference images.

Pythium reference shows very early-stage cotyledon rot in wet soil. Rhizoctonia shows dry firm cankers on older seedlings. Phytophthora top-left shows wilted young plants that look similar to the test. Let me check a couple more.
None of the others (Fusarium, SDS, Charcoal Rot) match — those all show more mature plants with stem/root symptoms. Let me look at one more to confirm.

Tobacco Streak Virus doesn't match — it shows pod and mature plant symptoms.

**Final analysis:**

The test image shows young soybean seedlings (early post-emergence stage) completely collapsed/wilted in sandy soil. Comparing all evidence:

- **Pythium**: Reference shows even earlier cotyledon-stage rot in wet dark soil — plants slightly less developed than test
- **Phytophthora**: Reference top-left shows nearly identical pattern — young seedlings collapsed/wilted in field conditions; description says "young plants show rapid yellowing, wilting, and soft rot collapse"
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows dry firm reddish-brown cankers at soil line on more developed plants — not matching the full collapse pattern
- **Fusarium/SDS/Charcoal Rot**: All show symptoms on more mature plants

The complete seedling collapse with yellowed/drooping leaves in a cluster, matching the Phytophthora reference image most closely, points to **Phytophthora**.
